# ui::ObservableVector

Header: `winui/core/ObservableVector.hpp`.

```cpp
template <typename T> class ObservableVector
```

Derives from `ui::PropertyBase`.

A collection that reports each edit: what was inserted, removed, replaced or moved, and where.

It is the collection counterpart of [ui::Property](property.md). A [Property](property.md) holding a `std::vector` can only say "changed"; an ObservableVector says what changed, so a [ui::ForEach](../controls/for-each.md#uiforeach) or a list view bound to it builds one row for an inserted item, destroys one for a removed item and leaves every other row, and its state, alone.

Each item lives at its own address, which stays the same for as long as the item is in the collection, whatever is inserted or removed around it. A row may therefore keep a reference to its item and bind to the item's own [Property](property.md) members. Positions do shift, so a row should not keep its index; [index_of()](#index_of) finds an item's current position.

Observers are held the same way a [Property](property.md) holds them: the collection or the observer may be destroyed first. Destroying the collection reports a Reset to empty, so a tree still showing it shows nothing afterwards. Non-copyable and non-movable; UI-thread only.

Example: 
```cpp
struct Todo
{
    explicit Todo(std::string text) : title{std::move(text)} {}
    ui::Property<std::string> title;
    ui::Property<bool>        done{false};
};
ui::ObservableVector<Todo> todos;

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
    ui::Button{.text = "Add", .on_click = [&] { todos.emplace_back("New task"); }},
    ui::ForEach<Todo>{
        .items = todos,
        .item  = [&todos](Todo& todo) -> ui::Spec
        {
            return ui::HorizontalStack{.spacing = 8, .content = {
                ui::ToggleSwitch{.checked = todo.done},
                ui::Text{.text = todo.title},
                ui::Button{.text = "Remove", .on_click = [&todos, &todo] { todos.remove(todo); }},
            }};
        },
    },
}});
```

## ObservableVector

```cpp
ObservableVector(std::initializer_list<T> items)
    requires std::copy_constructible<T>
```

Holds a copy of each of `items`; no observer exists yet, so nothing is notified.

## ~ObservableVector

```cpp
~ObservableVector()
```

Reports a Reset to empty, then leaves every remaining [Subscription](subscription.md) dead.

```cpp

```

True when the collection holds no items.

## count

```cpp
const Property<std::size_t>& count() const noexcept
```

How many items the collection holds, as a [Property](property.md), so a binding follows it: an empty-state text that shows while there is nothing, a count in a heading. It changes after the collection's own observers were told.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::ObservableVector<std::string> files;
window.set_content(ui::Text{
    .text    = "No files yet",
    .visible = ui::bind(files.count(), [](std::size_t n) { return n == 0; }),
});
```

## erase

```cpp
void erase(std::size_t index, std::size_t count = 1, std::source_location where = std::source_location::current())
```

Removes [`count`](#count) items starting at `index`; a range reaching past the end is cut short. The items are destroyed after the observers have been told.

## remove

```cpp
bool remove(const T& item, std::source_location where = std::source_location::current())
```

Removes `item`, found by its address. False when it is not an item of this collection.

## erase_if

```cpp
template <typename Predicate>
std::size_t erase_if(Predicate predicate, std::source_location where = std::source_location::current())
    requires std::predicate<Predicate&, const T&>
```

Removes every item for which `predicate` answers true, and returns how many went. Each run of neighboring matches is reported as one Removed, from the back of the collection to the front. `predicate` is asked about every item before the first one goes.

## replace

```cpp
T& replace(std::size_t index, T item, std::source_location where = std::source_location::current())
    requires std::move_constructible<T>
```

Replaces the item at `index` with `item`; whatever was built for the old one is built again. For an item that holds Properties, set those instead: nothing needs rebuilding.

## move

```cpp
void move(std::size_t from, std::size_t to, std::source_location where = std::source_location::current())
```

Moves the item at `from` to position `to`, both less than [size()](#size). The item keeps its address, and what was built for it stays as it is.

## clear

```cpp
void clear(std::source_location where = std::source_location::current())
```

Removes every item, reported as one Reset.

## assign

```cpp
template <typename Range>
void assign(const Range& items, std::source_location where = std::source_location::current())
    requires requires(const Range& range) { { *std::begin(range) } -> std::convertible_to<T>; }
```

Replaces the whole content with a copy of each of `items`, reported as one Reset. Nothing is reported when the collection was empty and stays empty.

## batch

```cpp
template <typename Edits>
void batch(Edits edits, std::source_location where = std::source_location::current())
    requires std::invocable<Edits&>
```

Runs `edits`, which edit this collection, and reports everything they did as one Reset when they return, instead of one change per edit. For a bulk edit (an undo step, a sort, a reload) whose rows are cheaper to build again once than to follow edit by edit. A batch inside a batch reports once, when the outermost returns. Items removed or replaced during the batch are destroyed after the Reset was reported, so nothing built for them dangles. Nothing is reported when `edits` changed nothing.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::ObservableVector<std::string> pages{"Intro", "Setup", "Usage", "Cover"};
pages.batch([&] {
    std::string moved = pages[3];
    pages.erase(3);
    pages.insert(0, std::move(moved));
});
```

## observe

```cpp
Subscription observe(Callback<void(const CollectionChange&)> fn) const
```

Observe changes. The returned [Subscription](subscription.md) must be kept alive for `fn` to keep firing; an [Element](../tree/element.md) keeps it with [Element::add_subscription()](../tree/element.md#add_subscription). `fn` runs after the collection has changed, and is not called for the current content.
